subject.title: CLI-backed helper paths still bypass CLI dispatch on latest main

question: Should CLI-backed helper parity be finished as narrow dispatch-boundary fixes under this umbrella, or should the remaining status/probe, slug-generation, and subagent/gateway surfaces be split into separate maintainer-owned issues before changing provider/runtime semantics?
rationale: The remaining paths cross auth-provider visibility, potential API-vs-CLI billing behavior, and persisted session metadata, so automation should not choose the long-term runtime boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: Keep Umbrella And Land Narrow Fixes
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers review narrow repairs for status/probe visibility, slug-generation dispatch, and subagent/gateway runtime handoff with live or source-backed proof.

options.title: Split Remaining Work
options.body: Close this umbrella only after linking canonical narrow issues for every remaining helper path and preserving the existing evidence there.

options.title: Defer CLI Helper Parity
options.body: Explicitly decide that some optional helpers may stay embedded/API-backed even when agent turns use CLI runtimes, documenting that operator-visible behavior.

recommendation.title: Keep Umbrella And Land Narrow Fixes
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers review narrow repairs for status/probe visibility, slug-generation dispatch, and subagent/gateway runtime handoff with live or source-backed proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent history shows the broadest cross-surface ownership across provider/runtime, status, slug, subagent, and gateway paths.
